This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place, no matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder. The Pentagon now says the execution of the former Army major who killed 13 people in a mass shooting at Fort Hood in 2009 will be live streamed.
The Pentagon says more details will follow after Defense Secretary Pete Hegcess said the execution would be public.
People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things.
Hegcess speaking Thursday to the conservative television outlet Real America's Voice. The Army says the execution of Nadal Hassan will take place at Fort Hood on December 3rd.
In addition to the 13 killed, more than 30 others were injured. The last widely recognized public execution in the United States took place in Kentucky in 1936.
Federal Reserve Governor Chris Waller says he expects the central bank to raise interest rates again to tamp down stubborn inflation.
But NPR's Scott Horsley reports that Waller sees the timing of a rate hike as flexible.
Speaking at a conference in Istanbul organized by Turkey's central bank, Waller said inflation in the U.S. has been too high for too long, and he's seen too little progress towards the Fed's inflation target of 2 percent.
Waller and his colleagues the Fed voted unanimously last month to raise their benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point. Waller says that's probably not the last rate hike that will be needed.
The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meeting, but they should be in place in an acceptable period of time.
Investors expect the Fed to hold its benchmark interest rates steady at this month's meeting with an increase likely when policymakers meet in December. Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
New York City Mayor Zara Mumdani is condemning federal immigration agents following a shooting late Thursday in Manhattan's Marble Hill neighborhood.
One person was wounded. Officials say an ICE agent fired several shots and that a young child was in the back seat of the suspect's car.
The suspect has been identified as a 28-year-old for the Dominican Republic. New York police say he's been arrested twice in the city.
Vice President J.D. Vance's nine universities, including Harvard, Yale, and Stanford, are being investigated for allegedly abusing a visa program for international students.
Here's NPR's Frankio Ordonez. Vance accused the nine universities, which also included the University of Pittsburgh, Brown, and MIT, with bringing in students and researchers under J-1 visas at a rate much higher than the national average.
So something weird is going on at these universities. They're using these visas way too much. They're using them to undercut the wages of American grad students and American researchers, and it simply has to stop.
Vance said the universities are replacing American graduate students who would be making $20,000 more than a researcher on a J-1 visa.
He called the actions a "insult to the American worker and to the American way of life." The administration said that subpoenas have already been served. Frankio Ordonez, NPR News, the White House.
This is NPR. President Trump's planned memorial arch is facing a new lawsuit. The Arlington County Board in Virginia filed the suit Thursday, becoming the first government body to take legal action.
The lawsuit cites what it says is a feverish pace toward construction and says it will harm public safety and likely require changes to nearby flight paths.
Despite some federal fuel relief measures, rising gas prices continue to put strain on drivers, especially those who depend on diesel. From Mississippi Public Radio, Elise Katrin Gregg reports.
At a gas station in Jackson, U.S. Senate candidate Scott Colombe called for a temporary suspension of the federal gas tax and a permanent stopgap for diesel relief.
He was joined by Arthur Payton, who owns a family trucking company based in Jackson, but they haul across the country. Payton says the price spikes are costing drivers up to $700 more every week in gas expenses.
The diesel cost at the pump now is averaging $6.30. That's about a $2.50 increase in just six-month period, and it's hard to recover those additional expenses in a short period of time.
Payton says they've started doing their own maintenance work on trucks to cut costs. For NPR News, I'm Elise Katrin Gregg in Jackson, Mississippi.
Ahead of the opening bell on Wall Street, the major financial markets in Europe are advancing as oil prices ease. Oil prices dipped 1 percent after President Trump said the U.S. will not attack Iran before next month's midterm election.
However, benchmark crude, the international standard, remains above $100 a barrel. I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
